cards.text: Isaiah the prophet opens with a woe for Ephraim, the kingdom that separated from Judah (Isaiah 7:17). Nobody ever opened a letter that starts with WOE and found a coupon inside. It's aimed at a majestic crown, set on the summit above the fertile valley, right up top where the whole valley can see it.

cards.question: Isaiah's woe is for the majestic crown of Ephraim's ___.
It's a woe, not a compliment. What kind of flower does Isaiah call the glorious splendor of Ephraim's crown?

cards.text: Then Isaiah says, "Behold, the Lord has one who is strong and mighty." Isaiah never says who. He just tells you how this one shows up.

cards.question: What does Isaiah say the Lord's strong and mighty one will be like?

answers.text: A fire spreading through the forest

cards.question: The Lord's strong and mighty one will lift Ephraim's crown even higher on the summit.

cards.text: That crown will be trampled underfoot. Top of the hill to the bottom of somebody's sandal, and then Isaiah gives that fading flower on the summit one more picture.

cards.question: What will the fading flower on the summit be like?

answers.text: A ripe fig before the summer harvest
Grass that withers in the noon sun
A reed shaken by the river wind

cards.question: Whoever sees that ripe fig will leave it hanging on the tree for later.

cards.text: One look, one grab, GONE, which is exactly me in front of a cooling rack, friend. Then the picture flips: on that day the LORD of Hosts Himself will be a crown of glory, a diadem of splendor.

cards.question: On that day, who will the LORD of Hosts be a crown of glory to?
The LORD will be a spirit of ___ to him who sits in judgment.
The LORD will also be a strength to those who repel the onslaught at the gate.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says these also stagger from wine and stumble from strong drink. The next names on that list nearly knocked me off my gold base, friend, and that thing is GLUED to me.

cards.question: Who does Isaiah say reels from strong drink and is befuddled by wine?
The strong drink leaves the priests and prophets muddled in their visions and stumbling in their judgments.

cards.text: Isaiah says it plainly: "For all their tables are covered with vomit; there is not a place without filth." Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer full of dust, and even I would not pull up a seat at those tables.
Then the questions come: "Whom is He trying to teach? To whom is He explaining His message?" I think somebody feels talked down to.

cards.question: The questions about whom He's trying to teach keep going. Which group do they name?

answers.text: Elders sitting at the city gate

cards.text: For they hear: "Order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line; a little here, a little there." That's the coworker who explains the copier one button at a time. EVERY. SINGLE. MORNING.

cards.question: Isaiah says He will speak to this people another way. How?

answers.text: With mocking lips and foreign tongues
By a voice from the clouds

cards.text: These are people He already spoke to, and He told them, "This is the place of rest, let the weary rest; this is the place of repose." Friend, I lay flat in a junk drawer for years and STILL never got rest like that.

cards.question: The people listened and took the rest He offered them.

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD to them will become that line again: order on order, line on line, a little here, a little there. The copier coworker is BACK, friend, and this time he brought laminated notes.

cards.question: When the word of the LORD becomes that line again, which way does it send the people?
Stumbling backward, they will be injured, ensnared and ___.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess a word of Isaiah 28:1 they haven't seen. Card 1 gives no context about wine or drinking, so 'drunkards' can't be reasoned out over 'shepherds' or 'kings', and 'kings' fits a crown at least as well. It is pure wording recall or luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences: the quote, 'Isaiah never says who.', and 'He just tells you how this one shows up.' Only the opening card may run to three.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Of the 7 choice cards in stop 2, 4 are multiple choice, 2 are true or false and only 1 is fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
